newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indonesian gas output seen up 10m tonnes on Natuna.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian gas output seen up 10m tonnes on Natuna.

text.p: Indonesia's liquefied natural gas output (LNG) is expected to increase by 10 million tonnes per year to 30 million tonnes when the Natuna gas project becomes productive, a senior Pertamina official said on Monday
The Natuna D-Alpha project in the East Natuna Sea was planned to come on stream in 2002, said G.A.S Nayoan, the senior executive Vice President of Executive Board, Natuna Project.

Indonesia supplies 53 percent of LNG demand in the Asia Pacific region with a current production of 20 million tonnes, Nayoan told reporters ahead of the the offshore Southeast Asia Conference and Exhibition due to start on Tuesday.
Gas consumption in the Asia Pacific region, around 53 million tonne per year, was expected to rise to 116 million tones a year in 2010, Nayoan said.
He said Pertamina was negotiating with a Japanese consortium which may take a 13 percent stake in Natuna gas project. He did not identify the members of the consortium.
Exxon Corp has a 50 percent stake in the project and Mobil oil a 26 percent interest. Pertamina, Indonesia's state-owned oil company, will eventually hold only 11 percent interest.
Nayoan told Reuters later that Pertamina last met the Japanese consortium earlier this month but discussion had not yet been finalised.
Negotiations are also underway with Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) on a potential pipeline project to pipe gas from Natuna field to Thailand.
Nayoan told reporters the initial phase of sales contracts for Natuna gas have a pipeline gas option.
"This option calls for a 1,538 kilometre-long submarine pipeline to Thailand and could well be the first leg a of Southeast Asian pipeline grid," he said.
Nayoan told Reuters PTT and Pertamina had made a "commitment" to the project by signing a memorandum of understanding in August.
"Potential sales contracts of the gas can be made for a period of 30 years," he said.
